answer.rationale: Current data shows activation and onboarding completion both declining 4–6% QoQ. Two prior experiments (memory_31: signup simplification lifted first-week activation in SMBs; memory_86: shortened onboarding improved completion rates) directly address this problem and have shown durable positive effects. Verifying these two will confirm the magnitude and durability of field reduction and onboarding streamlining before scaling. This approach avoids promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed -12pp early retention and is not sustainable), focuses on improving core product funnel health rather than chasing price-sensitive cohorts lost to competitor entry, and preserves the option to layer activation_messaging (memory_91) or enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) later. A standard_experiment scope on simplified onboarding is justified: the problem is measurable (4% dip in completion), the intervention is low-risk, and success unlocks sustainable volume without eroding unit economics. This also protects long-term qualified revenue by addressing the root funnel friction rather than discounting.
